Image size & uploads / FIELD GUIDE

How to resize a photo in pixels without stretching or blurring it

A photo can fit the exact pixel limit without looking squashed. The trick is to protect its proportions.

By Manglo Editorial7 November 20266 min read
THE MANGLO PLAYBOOK / ORIGINAL GUIDE

You have a photo that is 4,000 × 3,000 pixels. The upload page asks for something smaller. Should you enter 1,000 × 1,000? Not immediately: changing both numbers without considering the photo's original shape can make people and objects look stretched.

Understand pixels before you resize

Width × height is the number of picture elements across and down the image. KB or MB is the amount of storage the encoded file uses. They are related, but not interchangeable. Two images with identical dimensions can have very different file sizes because of their contents, format and compression settings.

Keep the aspect ratio

Aspect ratio is width divided by height. A 4,000 × 3,000 photo has a 4:3 ratio. To keep that shape at one-quarter scale, use 1,000 × 750 pixels, not 1,000 × 1,000. The same proportions are maintained, so a round object stays round.

New height = original height × (new width ÷ original width)

For our example: 3,000 × (1,000 ÷ 4,000) = 750 pixels. You can calculate the width from a target height in exactly the same way.

Resize in four steps

  1. Keep an untouched original file.
  2. Find the exact pixel requirement of the website, employer, form or social platform.
  3. Open the Manglo image resizer, upload the photo and enter the desired maximum dimensions.
  4. Leave Preserve aspect ratio enabled for a proportional fit, then download and inspect the result.

When aspect ratio is preserved, Manglo fits the image within the requested width and height. The final dimensions may be smaller than one of the numbers you entered. If a portal demands an exact square, crop to square first with the crop tool; stretching a rectangular photograph is not the answer.

Why a resized photo sometimes looks blurry

  • Enlarging a small source: adding pixels cannot recreate missing details.
  • Over-compression: a low-quality JPG export can soften fine lines.
  • Wrong crop: a subject that is tiny in the frame remains tiny after resizing.
  • Comparing at different zoom levels: judge the image at its real destination size.

Resize or compress—which one do you need?

RequirementStart with
“Max 800 × 800 pixels”Resize, preserving the required shape.
“Image under 200 KB”Target-size compression, after meeting dimension rules.
“Square image only”Crop to 1:1, then resize.

Always check the site's own current specifications. The 100 KB / 200 KB guide covers the next step if the dimensions are right but the file is still too heavy.

Further reading: web.dev on image dimensions and formats.
